title: ProjectE loop-gain stability margins
description: Output of tools/scripts/sim/loop_stability.py. It reads a loop-gain response somebody else produced - an AC simulation or a network analyser - and does arithmetic on it. Locating a 0 dB crossing and measuring the phase there is not proprietary, which is what lets this run without a vendor's compensation model in hand; the acceptance thresholds ARE specific, and are therefore inputs rather than numbers invented here.

models_the_loop.description: A regulator vendor's compensation network is theirs and is not reproduced, approximated or guessed. This artifact carries measurements of a response, not a model of one.

band_hz.description: The swept band. A response that never reaches 0 dB inside it has no margin to report - which is NO_COVERAGE, not a pass, and not an extrapolation problem to solve.

phase_wraps_removed.description: Reported as evidence that unwrapping happened. A margin computed from wrapped phase is confidently wrong rather than obviously wrong, because it still lands in a plausible range; a reader looking at the margin alone cannot tell the two apart.

gain_crossings.description: EVERY 0 dB crossing, not the first. A loop can cross several times and is only as good as its worst crossing; reporting one phase margin discards the rest.

bracket_decades.description: How far apart the samples either side of the crossing were. A crossover printed to four digits from decade-spaced samples is a false precision; the bracket travels with the number so the reader can see it.

above_unity.description: True when gain is still above 0 dB where phase passes -180 deg. That loop is stable as built and unstable if the gain FALLS - the direction it moves as parts age, as ceramics lose value to DC bias, and at light load. A phase margin taken at crossover cannot see this and looks fine.

budget.description: Acceptance thresholds. Both null means the margins were computed but nothing judged them, and the run is NO_COVERAGE.
